India Moves to Restrict Junk Food Sales Within 50 Metres of Schools

India is progressing with plans to implement restrictions on the sale of junk food items in close proximity to schools. The proposed measure intends to prohibit the sale of such foods within a 50-meter radius of educational institutions. The move is primarily aimed at creating a more conducive environment for children and adolescents to make healthier food choices during their school day. By limiting convenient access to processed and unhealthy food options near campuses, authorities are seeking to mitigate the consumption of items typically high in sugar, salt, and unhealthy fats, which are often linked to various public health challenges.

The Economist: India’s education system faces crisis beyond leaky roofs

The Economist reports that India’s education system is confronting a crisis that extends far beyond the well‑documented problem of leaky school roofs. While infrastructure decay remains visible, the publication highlights deeper issues such as uneven resource allocation, chronic teacher shortages and gaps in curriculum relevance. It notes that enrolment figures have risen dramatically, yet learning outcomes lag, with many students completing primary school without mastering basic literacy and numeracy. The analysis points to a mismatch between funding formulas and on‑ground needs, suggesting that money is often spent on cosmetic repairs rather than on teacher training, digital tools or curriculum updates. The article also references recent government initiatives aimed at upgrading facilities, but stresses that without parallel reforms in assessment standards and accountability mechanisms, physical repairs alone will not resolve the systemic weakness. The Economist calls for coordinated policy action that links funding to measurable improvements in student performance, urging state‑level audits and a transparent reporting framework. What to watch: upcoming Ministry of Education budget revisions and the rollout of the National Education Policy reforms.
